title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 41-42
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 41 to 42 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'उद्भवः क्षोभणो देवः श्रीगर्भः परमेश्वरः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 41 to 42 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 41 to 42.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 41 to 42** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **उद्भवः क्षोभणो देवः श्रीगर्भः परमेश्वरः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**उद्भवः क्षोभणो देवः श्रीगर्भः परमेश्वरः । करणं कारणं कर्ता विकर्ता गहनो गुहः ॥** **व्यवसायो व्यवस्थानः संस्थानः स्थानदो ध्रुवः । परर्द्धिः परमस्पष्टस्तुष्टः पुष्टः शुभेक्षणः ॥**

He is the source of everything, he stirs the world, a shining God. The supreme Lord who holds Shri within himself is that God of gods. The means, the cause, the doer, the one who transforms, the unfathomable, dwelling in the cave of the heart. He is resolve itself, the one who orders all things, gives each its place and stays unmoved. Of supreme glory, utterly clear, content, the nourisher with a kind gaze, is that God of gods.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 41 to 42 mean?
faq.a: He is the source of everything, he stirs the world, a shining God. The supreme Lord who holds Shri within himself is that God of gods. The means, the cause, the doer, the one who transforms, the unfathomable, dwelling in the cave of the heart. He is resolve itself, the one who orders all things, gives each its place and stays unmoved. Of supreme glory, utterly clear, content, the nourisher with a kind gaze, is that God of gods.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
